structured_output.summary: The governance correction set is architecturally strong: `tools/postdelivery.py` proves the published 0.2.4 payload is byte/mode-identical to commit 6f18529 outside a tested allowlist, the maintained observer now rejects a newer failure/pending run with two agreeing bounded snapshots, and all six remote-delivery attempt-2 findings plus readiness attempt-4 findings 1–2 are implemented with real negative tests. Authorization is explicit and pinned, and the limitations document is honest. But the changed CI route cannot pass: `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:80` reads `report["phase"]`/`source_unchanged`, which `qualify_portable` never writes (confirmed in the produced receipt), and no test covers it. Attempt-5 check evidence is also governance-scoped only — the readiness commands are hash-bound from another worktree, never re-executed against the changed guards. One prior required fix remains unimplemented.

findings.description: The governance CI route writes docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json via postdelivery.qualify_portable (tools/postdelivery.py:356-368), whose report keys are exactly passed, source_sha256, qualifiedSourceSha256, scope, registryArchiveSha256, limitation, checks, hostQualificationSha256 (verify_portable return, tools/postdelivery.py:351-353). The receipt-logging step still indexes report["phase"] and report["source_unchanged"], which the old check_phase --contracts-only report supplied but this one does not. The produced artifact confirms this: docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json has no "phase" or "source_unchanged" key anywhere (only hostQualificationSha256 at :122). The step raises KeyError and fails the contracts-and-package job, so the newly wired governance workflow cannot pass on push. No test catches it: tools/test_ci.py:161-166 only counts the command occurrence, :575-578 only assert the filename, and :194 permits the governance flag in the gate regex.
findings.required_fix: Either emit phase/source_unchanged from postdelivery.verify_portable (and record them in the report) or change .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:80 to print the keys the governance report actually contains (for example scope, source_sha256, qualifiedSourceSha256, passed). Add a tools/test_ci.py regression that parses the heredoc's requested key tuple and asserts it is a subset of the keys qualify_portable writes, then re-run the portable route to rebind docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json.

findings.description: For a phase-28 chunk record carrying qualification_scope=post_publication_governance, check_evidence bypasses the commands_for(28) comparison entirely and delegates to postdelivery.verify_governance_checks, so this readiness chunk attempt accepts the 8-command governance set (docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-05.checks.json:72-200) as its passing evidence. The readiness criteria PHASES.md:291-298 names — the 105-command cumulative gate, both --require-directional package proofs, and the 0.2.4 candidate/prepublication guards — are only hash-bound from the external root /home/cdot/development/cdot65/scm-sdk-rs-ts035 (postdelivery.py:185-212) and were executed at source f9cebee, not at the reviewed source 2a2984e. Because tools/release_delivery.py, tools/check_phase.py, tools/review_phase.py and scripts/observe-release.py are all in GOVERNANCE_PATHS (postdelivery.py:17-23), the changed guards themselves are covered in this tree only by unit tests; verify_composed deliberately runs the qualified root's older release_delivery.py (postdelivery.py:218-222).
findings.required_fix: State this boundary explicitly in the chunk record and in docs/post-publication-governance.md (the readiness chunk's attempt-5 evidence is payload-equivalence plus governance tests, not a re-executed readiness gate), or re-execute the registered phase-28 command set in the governance checkout so the changed guards are qualified against the current source rather than only unit-tested.

findings.description: Readiness attempt-4 finding 2 required the mirror push authorization and the fourth delivery receipt to be recorded in the AGENTS.md push-destination clause as well as PHASES.md and the plan. PHASES.md:306-312, docs/typescript-035-parity-plan.md:160-166 and docs/RELEASE.md were updated and are now asserted by tools/test_release_024.py:57-61, but AGENTS.md:13 still states a single authorized push destination (ssh://git@git-ssh.cdot.io/...) with no mention of the GitHub mirror, the fourth receipt, or the full-reachable-history disclosure. AGENTS.md is also absent from postdelivery.GOVERNANCE_PATHS (tools/postdelivery.py:17-23), so the fix is structurally impossible in this checkout — the immutable inventory would reject it.
findings.required_fix: Either add AGENTS.md to the governance allowlist and record the mirror destination, fourth delivery receipt and history-exposure disclosure in its push-destination clause (asserting the sentences in tools/test_release_024.py alongside the PHASES/plan phrases), or document in docs/post-publication-governance.md that this part of the finding is deferred to a checkout where AGENTS.md is mutable, and say so in the chunk record.

findings.description: Readiness attempt-4 finding 3 asked for the packaged README link to be derived from release_delivery.GITHUB_REMOTE and the crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml version. The new assertion hardcodes the full literal URL instead, so the stale-link risk it was meant to close remains: bumping the crate version while leaving README.md:31 at blob/v0.2.4 still passes, and a mirror-host change is not checked against GITHUB_REMOTE.
findings.required_fix: Derive the expected URL from release_delivery.GITHUB_REMOTE and the Cargo.toml version and assert README.md contains exactly that blob/v<version>/docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md link.

findings.description: immutable_inventory compares the symmetric difference minus the allowlist, then iterates only over (baseline | current) - allowed. Deleting an allowlisted governance file (for example tools/release_delivery.py or .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml) therefore passes the inventory check unnoticed; only downstream import or read failures would surface it. test_only_explicit_governance_paths_may_change (tools/test_postdelivery.py:96-107) covers modification and new unapproved files, not deletion.
findings.required_fix: Require every GOVERNANCE_PATHS entry present in the baseline to still exist as a regular file, and add a deletion case to test_only_explicit_governance_paths_may_change.

evidence: Published-payload immutability is enforced, not asserted: tools/postdelivery.py:53-91 rebuilds every blob OID and mode from `git ls-tree 6f18529`, compares against `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, rejects symlinks/replacements, and permits divergence only for the 19 explicit GOVERNANCE_PATHS (:17-23); the workflow is additionally pinned to exactly the contracts-route/report-name substitution (:70-77). tools/test_postdelivery.py:58-107 proves rejection of changed Rust/contract/lock/README bytes, a new payload file, a payload symlink, and an unapproved tools/ file. The governance allowlist equals the executed suite list by test (:364-375).

Remote-delivery attempt-2 findings are implemented with real negative coverage. Original vs fresh CI receipt separation: docs/phase-status.json:8971-8974 keeps delivery.ci_receipt (phase-28-remote-ci-run-31.json) distinct from ci_observation (…-observation-03.json), and postdelivery.py:227-231 requires the fresh observation to retain the original sourceCommit/run. Two agreeing bounded snapshots with an observation window: scripts/observe-release.py:237-248 captures statuses and run history twice and fails on any change; verify_status_snapshot:158-175 requires both confirmation digests, start<=confirm<=end, and checkedAt>=end. A later non-success run cannot be hidden: :162 requires history[-1] == run with status success, exercised by tools/test_release_023.py:245-291 (later-failure, later-pending, changed-history, appended run43) plus equal-timestamp and across-pages selection and a token-leak assertion (:292).

Retained guard and prior-failure validation now exist: tools/postdelivery.py:135-147 re-executes the canonical guard in the qualified root and requires docs/checks/phase-28-composed-delivery-F.json to match command, cwd, exit code, parsed result and both stream digests, with seven tamper subtests (tools/test_postdelivery.py:377-398); :150-171 pins the run-30 failure identity (counts {success:48, failure:1}, html_url, index 30) and requires it in both observed run histories, with four rejection cases (:400-441).

Fresh post-publication observations are bound to the reviewed source: docs/checks/release-tag-github-v0.2.4-observation-03.json:12-16 records qualifiedSourceSha256 f9cebee…, publishedSourceCommit 6f18529…, governanceSourceSha256 2a2984e… (equal to this review's source) and observerSha256; postdelivery.verify_tag_observations:101-132 requires remote, annotated peeled ref, equality with the original tagObject, the current observer hash, and checkedAt >= registry publishedAt, with tampering rejected at tools/test_postdelivery.py:316-333.

The readiness chain that preceded publication is real and ordered: docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-04.json:6-13,70 is accepted at 44/50 on source f9cebee with 105 executed commands; docs/checks/phase-28.json:2-7 is phase 28, source f9cebee, passed true; docs/reviews/phase-28-attempt-05.json:68-80 is the release_readiness-scope review accepted_with_deficiencies at 44 with every category >=8, matching gate_decision's documented fifth-attempt exception (tools/review_phase.py:121-124). Tag-before-publish ordering is now both documented and asserted (tools/test_release_024.py:62-65).

Review-budget integrity is explicit, not inferred: tools/review_phase.py:67-94 validates the exact grant id, question call id and answer in docs/reviews/recovery-authorizations/2026-10-22.json:21-35 and pins all 20 original readiness artifacts to FINAL_DELIVERY_ORIGINALS_SHA256; the separate namespace requires >=46/50 with no fifth-attempt exception (:695). tools/test_final_delivery_review.py uses a synthetic git root and patched originals digest so no real record is touched.

Confirmed defect: docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json contains only passed, source_sha256, qualifiedSourceSha256, scope, registryArchiveSha256, limitation, checks and hostQualificationSha256 (:1-8,:122) — a grep for "phase" and "source_unchanged" returns nothing — while .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:80 indexes both keys.

Attempt-5 check evidence is governance-scoped: docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-05.checks.json:2 declares scope post_publication_governance, and its only checks are seven unittest suites plus one composed guard invocation (:72-200, all exit_code 0, 150 focused tests). Its hostQualificationSha256 in the portable report (5c1439b4…) matches the prompt's declared checks digest, so the host report and the chunk evidence are the same bytes.

Payload equivalence and archived receipt identity are taken from postdelivery.py's logic and the recorded report.
